# Cement Mix Spec

**Department:** Production
**Scope:** Batching plant floor operations

## Purpose

Defines batching plant procedure for standard OPC (Ordinary Portland Cement)
production runs on Line 2 and Line 3.

## Batching sequence

1. Charge coarse aggregate, then 60% of mix water
2. Add cement and supplementary cementitious material
3. Add remaining water with admixture pre-diluted
4. Wet mix minimum 90 seconds after final water addition

## Equipment tolerances

| Parameter | Target | Tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| Cement weigh hopper | setpoint | ±1.0% |
| Aggregate weigh hopper | setpoint | ±2.0% |
| Water meter | setpoint | ±1.0% |
| Mixer discharge temperature | 28°C | ±4°C |

## Operator checks per shift

- Calibrate load cells at shift start; log to batching sheet
- Verify moisture probe reading against oven-dry sample once per shift
- Reject any batch where wet mix time falls below 90 s

## Escalation

Out-of-tolerance weigh hopper: stop the line, notify shift supervisor,
raise a maintenance ticket before resuming.

# Cement Mix Spec

**Department:** R&D
**Scope:** Laboratory trial formulations, low-carbon programme

## Purpose

Records experimental binder formulations under evaluation for clinker factor
reduction. **Not approved for production use.**

## Trial formulations

| Trial ID | Clinker % | Limestone filler % | Calcined clay % | 28-day strength (MPa) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| LC-11 | 65 | 20 | 15 | 42.1 |
| LC-14 | 55 | 15 | 30 | 39.6 |
| LC-19 | 50 | 20 | 30 | 36.2 |

## Test method

Mortar bars cast per lab SOP, cured in saturated lime water at 23°C.
Compressive strength measured at 3, 7, 28 and 90 days, three specimens per age.

## Observations

- LC-14 reaches acceptable 28-day strength with a 45% clinker reduction
- LC-19 shows extended setting time; retarder dosage needs re-evaluation
- Calcined clay above 30% degrades workability sharply at constant w/b

## Status

LC-14 recommended for pilot-scale trial. LC-19 on hold pending admixture study.

# Safety Guidelines

**Department:** Plant Operations
**Scope:** Kiln and clinker cooler areas

## Mandatory PPE

- Flame-resistant coveralls in the kiln hood zone
- Face shield plus safety glasses when observing burner flame
- Heat-resistant gloves rated to 250°C for cooler grate work

## Hot work restrictions

- No entry into the kiln shell within 48 hours of shutdown
- Confined space permit required for preheater cyclone entry
- Two-person rule inside the clinker cooler at all times

## Heat stress management

Rotate personnel out of the kiln floor every 30 minutes when ambient exceeds
40°C. Provide electrolyte fluids at the shift station.

## Emergency

Hot meal spill or kiln flush: evacuate to the upwind muster point, do not
attempt cleanup until the area is declared cool by the shift supervisor.

# Safety Guidelines

**Department:** Laboratory
**Scope:** Chemical handling and analytical instruments

## Chemical handling

- Hydrofluoric acid for XRF prep: fume hood only, calcium gluconate gel on hand
- Store concentrated acids in the ventilated corrosives cabinet, never above
  eye level
- Segregate oxidisers from organic solvents

## Fume hood requirements

Verify face velocity of 0.5 m/s before starting any acid digestion. Do not
store apparatus inside the hood; it disrupts airflow.

## Instrument safety

- XRF: interlock must be verified weekly; never bypass the sample chamber switch
- Muffle furnace: tongs and face shield above 500°C, no plastic near the door

## Spill response

Acid spill under 100 mL: neutralise with sodium bicarbonate, then absorb.
Over 100 mL or any HF spill: evacuate the lab and call the EHS duty officer.

# Concrete Mix Ratio Standard

**Version:** 2020-R1
**Effective:** 2020-03-01
**Status:** SUPERSEDED by 2024-R3
**Department:** Production

## Standard mix designs

| Grade | Cement : Sand : Aggregate | Max w/c ratio | 28-day target |
|---|---|---|---|
| C20 | 1 : 2 : 4 | 0.60 | 20 MPa |
| C25 | 1 : 1.5 : 3 | 0.55 | 25 MPa |
| C30 | 1 : 1.5 : 3 | 0.50 | 30 MPa |
| C40 | 1 : 1 : 2 | 0.45 | 40 MPa |

## Supplementary cementitious materials

Fly ash permitted up to **25%** cement replacement for C20–C30.
Not permitted for C40 or above.

## Curing

Minimum 7 days moist curing for all grades. Extend to 10 days when ambient
exceeds 35°C.

## Slump

Target 75–100 mm for general structural work. Do not retemper with water on site.

## Testing

Three cubes per 50 m³ placed, tested at 7 and 28 days.

# Concrete Mix Ratio Standard

**Version:** 2024-R3
**Effective:** 2024-11-01
**Status:** CURRENT — supersedes 2020-R1
**Department:** Production

## Standard mix designs

| Grade | Cement : Sand : Aggregate | Max w/c ratio | 28-day target |
|---|---|---|---|
| C20 | 1 : 2 : 4 | 0.58 | 20 MPa |
| C25 | 1 : 1.5 : 3 | 0.52 | 25 MPa |
| C30 | 1 : 1.5 : 3 | 0.48 | 30 MPa |
| C40 | 1 : 1 : 2 | 0.42 | 40 MPa |
| C50 | 1 : 1 : 1.8 | 0.38 | 50 MPa |

## Supplementary cementitious materials

Fly ash permitted up to **35%** cement replacement for C20–C30 (raised from 25%
in 2020-R1). Calcined clay blends permitted up to 30% for C20–C25 following the
2023 low-carbon programme.

Ground granulated blast-furnace slag now permitted up to 50% for marine exposure.

## Curing

Minimum 7 days moist curing. Extend to 14 days when ambient exceeds 35°C
(revised from 10 days).

## Slump

Target 75–100 mm general structural. Superplasticiser required for all
w/c below 0.45 — retempering with water remains prohibited.

## Testing

Three cubes per 50 m³ placed, tested at 7 and 28 days. Additional 56-day test
required for any mix using more than 30% SCM replacement.

## Changes from 2020-R1

- All w/c ratio caps tightened
- C50 grade added
- Fly ash limit raised 25% → 35%
- Hot-weather curing extended 10 → 14 days

# Clinker Production Process

**Department:** Production

## Raw meal preparation

Limestone and clay are crushed to under 25 mm, proportioned by the online
analyser, and ground in the vertical roller mill to a residue of 12–15% on the
90 µm sieve.

## Pyroprocessing

Raw meal passes through a five-stage preheater tower into the precalciner,
where roughly 90–95% calcination occurs before kiln entry. The rotary kiln
sinters the meal at a burning zone temperature of about 1450°C to form clinker
nodules.

## Kiln control parameters

| Parameter | Normal range |
|---|---|
| Burning zone temperature | 1420–1480°C |
| Kiln speed | 3.2–4.0 rpm |
| Back-end O2 | 2.5–3.5% |
| Free lime in clinker | 0.8–1.5% |

## Cooling

Grate cooler drops clinker from ~1350°C to below 100°C. Rapid cooling preserves
C3S and prevents C2S conversion.

## Common faults

- Rising free lime: check burning zone temperature and raw meal fineness
- Coating loss in burning zone: review flame shape and alkali/sulfur ratio
- Cooler snowman formation: inspect grate air distribution

# Business Unit Overview

**Department:** Corporate

## Structure

The group is organised into three primary business units.

### Cement and Building Materials
Cement, ready-mixed concrete, aggregates, roofing, ceramic tiles, and
sanitary ware. Largest unit by headcount.

### Chemicals
Olefins, polyolefins, PVC and downstream polymer products. Serves packaging,
automotive and construction customers.

### Packaging
Integrated pulp, paper, containerboard and flexible packaging solutions.

## Support functions

Logistics, international trading, and corporate R&D operate across all three
units rather than reporting into any single one.

## Customer segments

Construction contractors, building material retailers, FMCG manufacturers
(packaging), and industrial converters (chemicals).

# Packaging Materials Spec

**Department:** Packaging

## Containerboard grades

| Grade | Basis weight (g/m²) | Burst index | Typical use |
|---|---|---|---|
| KA125 | 125 | 3.2 | Outer liner, light duty |
| KA150 | 150 | 3.6 | Outer liner, standard |
| KA185 | 185 | 4.1 | Heavy duty / export |
| CM112 | 112 | — | Fluting medium |

## Cement bag specification

Multi-wall kraft paper sacks, 2-ply for 50 kg fill weight, valve type.
Minimum drop test: 6 drops from 1.2 m, no rupture.

Moisture barrier layer required for coastal and export shipment.

## Storage

Store paper reels at 50–60% RH. Below 40% RH the sheet embrittles and creases
crack during conversion.

# Python Coding Standards

**Department:** Engineering

## Style

- Formatter: `ruff format`, line length 100
- Linter: `ruff check` with the E, F, I, UP, B rule sets enabled
- Type hints required on all public functions; `mypy --strict` on new modules

## Project layout

Use `src/` layout with `pyproject.toml`. Dependencies pinned via `uv.lock`;
never commit a bare `requirements.txt` for a new service.

## Error handling

- Never use a bare `except:` — catch specific exception types
- Do not swallow exceptions silently; log with context or re-raise
- Use `contextlib.suppress` only where the ignored case is genuinely expected

## Testing

`pytest`, minimum 70% line coverage on new code. Fixtures over setUp methods.
Mark slow integration tests with `@pytest.mark.slow`.

## Logging

Structured logging via `structlog`. Never log credentials, API keys, or
customer PII.

# Data Pipeline Error Handling

**Department:** Engineering

## Retry policy

Transient failures (network, 5xx, timeout) retry with exponential backoff:
3 attempts, base delay 2 s, jitter enabled. Do not retry 4xx client errors.

## Idempotency

Every pipeline stage must be safe to re-run. Key writes on a deterministic
`run_id + partition_key` so a replay overwrites rather than duplicates.

## Dead letter handling

Records failing after all retries go to the DLQ topic with the original payload
plus `error_type`, `stage`, and `traceback`. DLQ is reviewed daily.

## Common Python exceptions in pipelines

| Exception | Usual cause | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `KeyError` | Upstream schema drift | Validate against schema registry first |
| `pandas.errors.ParserError` | Malformed CSV delimiter | Quarantine file, alert source owner |
| `TimeoutError` | Slow downstream API | Retry with backoff, then DLQ |
| `MemoryError` | Unbounded read | Switch to chunked iteration |

## Alerting

Page on-call only when DLQ depth exceeds 100 records or a stage fails 3
consecutive scheduled runs.

# Office and Site Locations

**Department:** Corporate Facilities

## Head office

Bangkok head office — main administrative functions, corporate R&D centre
on the same campus.

## Manufacturing sites

| Site | Type | Region |
|---|---|---|
| Site A | Integrated cement plant | Central |
| Site B | Cement grinding station | Northeast |
| Site C | Ready-mix batching hub | Eastern seaboard |
| Site D | Packaging converting plant | Central |

## Visitor access

All plant visits require 48 hours advance notice and a site safety induction
on arrival. Closed-toe shoes and long trousers are mandatory at every
manufacturing site.

## Shuttle service

Head office to Site A shuttle departs 07:00 and 13:00 on weekdays.

# IT Helpdesk FAQ

**Department:** IT

## Password reset

Self-service reset via the intranet portal. Passwords expire every 90 days.
Three failed attempts lock the account for 15 minutes.

## VPN access

Request through your line manager. Approval typically takes one business day.
VPN is required for any access to internal systems from outside the office network.

## Software requests

Standard software (Office, browsers, PDF tools) is pre-approved and installs
from the software centre. Anything else requires a ticket with business
justification.

## Reporting an incident

Raise a ticket in the service desk portal. For anything involving suspected
phishing or data loss, call the security hotline immediately rather than
emailing.

## Hardware refresh

Laptops are refreshed on a 4-year cycle. Early replacement requires a fault
report from IT support.
